reason: The cited evidence shows Mo addition causing σ phase precipitation and strengthening in a bcc Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ni HEA (E2), and thermal aging inducing L12 precipitates in an fcc AlCoCrFeNi HEA (E1). However, neither study involves a Ti-Ni-based HEA, so the key premises that Mo addition and 700°C aging will produce nano-scale precipitates and strengthening in this specific system are unsupported by direct prior evidence.
premises: Mo addition promotes precipitation of strengthening phases in HEAs
Thermal aging at 700°C for 5 hours induces nano-scale precipitates in Ti-Ni HEAs
Nano-scale precipitates hinder dislocation motion and enhance yield strength at elevated temperature
The specific Ti-Ni HEA system responds to Mo addition and aging similarly to the cited alloy systems
